om9-core geometry: Geometry::validate(&Limits) is the typed verdict for whether a geometry is usable

gap_found_by_this_task: There was no SuperSelect at all: no filter vocabulary and no way to ask 'which objects are gems' other than looking at names or colours — exactly what the negative oracle forbids.

Added superselect.rs: SelectFilter (Gems/BadGeometry/OpenGeometry/Duplicate), SkipReason for every object that does not match, classify() and Controller::superselect/apply_superselect. Gems match only the typed om9.gem slot; bad geometry matches only the model's own validate verdict; the open filter reports NoOpenVerdict instead of guessing.
RED is API-level and stated as such: the module did not exist. The fixtures (G1..G5, H1..H5) pin the rule, and H1/H2 are the exact trap the plan names (same label, gem-like look, no semantics).
reuse_decision: ADAPT the 'walk the model and gather' technique; ADD the typed filter vocabulary and the explicit skip reasons.
